  • 8+ years of direct Product Management experience.
  • Experience owning a platform, API or developer product that other teams or partners built on, and driving its adoption.
  • Technical fluency in APIs, data models and system design, with experience leading a migration to a new API or interface and credibility with senior engineers.
  • Strong platform judgment: you can decide what the shared system should and shouldn’t do, and make thoughtful choices about contracts and other decisions that are difficult to reverse.

  • Experience leading multi-team work across engineering, design and data, and connecting platform metrics to customer outcomes. Payroll, payments, tax or fintech experience is a plus, not required; we’ll teach the domain.

You’ll also collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Legal to surface trends, close gaps, and continuously improve the participant experience.

If you’re naturally curious, calm under pressure, and genuinely motivated by helping people navigate their financial futures, this role is for you.

About the Team:

At Gusto Retirement, customer care isn’t a support function — it’s a competitive advantage. Our Participant Support team is on the front lines of the 401(k) experience, serving as trusted advocates for the employees who depend on us most.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Deliver exceptional Tier 2 support. Serve as the in-depth resource for complex participant inquiries — going above and beyond via phone and email to resolve issues and build lasting trust.
  • Own the participant lifecycle. Be the go-to expert for the full participant experience at Gusto Retirement, with a focus on escalated and sensitive cases.
  • Manage your queue with intention. Balance inbound phone and email support, prioritizing by urgency while consistently hitting quality benchmarks — CSAT, response time, and resolution rate.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally. Partner with Sales, Engineering, Operations, and Legal to troubleshoot complex issues and deliver the best possible outcomes for participants.
  • Identify and surface trends. Spot patterns in participant feedback, flag gaps, and share actionable insights with internal teams to drive product and process improvements.
  • Navigate tools with confidence. Manage multiple platforms simultaneously — Notion, Jira, Salesforce, and Slack — while handling sensitive information with the utmost care.
  • Handle sensitive conversations with care. Bring empathy and active listening to difficult situations, finding paths to resolution that reflect Gusto’s values.
  • Report to the Customer Support Manager.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 2+ years of experience in customer care, customer success, relationship management, or FinTech
  • Experience in Benefits, 401(k), Payroll, or HR Tech is a plus
  • Results-driven with strong phone, listening, and writing skills — you’re a clear, confident communicator across every channel

descriptionHtml:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

Head of Risk & Money Services

At Gusto, we help more than 500,000 small businesses create great places to work for their people. We do this through modern payroll, employee benefits, expert HR, and financial services.

We are searching for a seasoned financial services operator and regulated-domain leader to own one of Gusto's most consequential customer-facing functions: Risk & Money Services. This role sits within CX and Gusto's Financial Services organization and reports directly to the Head of Financial Services.

Every dollar that moves through Gusto's platform — payroll being delivered on time, wages being deposited into Gusto Wallet, cash advances being issued, disputes being resolved — carries real financial and regulatory weight. Risk & Money Services is the team that protects this trust at the most critical edges of money movement: fraud and payment risk decisioning, Reg E dispute operations, collections, and the consumer money products that sit at the intersection of and its small business mission.

This function spans three interconnected practices:

  • Risk Operations — fraud ops, account takeover detection, payment-risk decisioning, and collections across both employer and employee money movement. This team makes real-time, high-stakes decisions on whether payroll goes out when something looks wrong, BSA/AML compliance, whether a fund recovery effort can be executed in time, and whether a fraud signal warrants action. The financial impact of individual calls is material. Focusing on risk mitigation and exceptional service is no easy task
  • Dispute Operations — Reg E dispute processing across Gusto's banking and money-movement products, from intake through resolution and provisional credit decisioning. This team owns Gusto's most regulated customer-facing process and operates at the intersection of customer trust and regulatory obligation.
  • Money Services and Banking — the operational home for Gusto Wallet, Cash Advance, and Gusto's expanding consumer financial products. This team is responsible for building the operational infrastructure that supports Gusto's growth in consumer banking — while protecting the customers who depend on it.

You will lead this organization through a senior leadership team, who carry full ownership for their function's outcomes, not just execution within it.Partner deeply with Compliance, Legal, Engineering, and Product across Gusto's products, and serve as the operational owner of the functions that sit at the regulated edge of Gusto's financial platform

This is a builder's role. Risk & Money Services is being stood up as a defined function within a new domain — you will set the SLAs, design the controls, build the metrics framework, establish the governance, and create the playbook that lets Gusto move money with confidence and scale.

Our mission is to create a world where work empowers a better life, and it starts right here at Gusto. That's why we're committed to building a collaborative and inclusive workplace, both physically and virtually.

Here's what you'll do

  • Own Risk & Money Services end to end. Be the single accountable leader for fraud and payment risk decisioning, BSA/AML compliance, Reg E dispute operations, collections, and the operational backbone of Gusto's money products. Own the customer experience, the regulatory posture, and the financial outcomes across this entire function.
  • Lead a multi-disciplinary regulated financial services organization through leaders who lead. Direct an organization spanning risk operations, dispute and fraud operations, and consumer money — through leaders who own their function end to end, whom you'll continue to develop, hire, and scale. Be the keeper of quality, speed, and regulatory integrity across all three practices.
  • Stand up Risk & Money Services as a defined operational function. Define the governance, the metrics framework, the SLAs, and the reporting infrastructure for a function that is being formalized for the first time. Build the operating muscle — controls documentation, audit readiness, workforce management, and escalation frameworks — that makes this domain run with the reliability a regulated function requires.
  • Own the highest-stakes real-time financial decisions in Gusto's customer operations. Be accountable for the decisions your team makes every day on whether payroll goes out when something looks wrong, whether a dispute warrants provisional credit, whether a fraud signal warrants action, and whether a fund recovery effort can be executed in time. These decisions carry material financial impact for customers and for Gusto — and they happen in real time.
  • Own Gusto's Reg E compliance posture at the operational level. Lead the operational program that governs Gusto's Reg E dispute obligations — intake, investigation, provisional credit, resolution, and customer communication — in partnership with Compliance and Legal. Ensure the team's practices are auditable, scalable, and consistently defensible.
  • Lead BSA/AML operational response. Own the customer-facing operational work triggered by BSA/AML alert activity — transaction monitoring response, customer outreach, account action — in partnership with Gusto's Compliance program. Ensure operational response meets the timeliness and documentation standards required by Gusto's sponsor bank relationships and regulatory obligations.
  • Build Consumer Money for growth. Own the operational infrastructure for Gusto Wallet, Cash Advance, and Gusto's expanding consumer financial product suite. Build the SOPs, workforce model, controls, and SLAs that support consumer product growth while protecting the customers who depend on these products.
  • Drive AI-native transformation in a regulated financial domain. Partner with Gusto's shared service platform and AI organization to bring AI agents, semantic knowledge, and automation capabilities into Risk & Money Services — accelerating fraud decisioning speed, dispute throughput, and risk signal accuracy while protecting the regulatory accountability this domain requires.
  • Be the operational counterpart to Product, Engineering, and Risk partners. Operate as the direct customer experience and operational owner across Gusto's money and risk product organizations — translating the operational and regulatory reality of risk and money movement into product priorities, and translating product roadmap into operational and regulatory readiness.
  • Represent Risk & Money Services externally. Be the direct voice with Gusto's sponsor bank partners, regulators, and auditors on matters affecting risk and money movement — not just the internal operator of the controls they require, but the leader they know and deal with directly.
  • Build the playbook for new financial products. Establish Risk & Money Services as the operational home for the risk and money movement functions of Gusto's growing financial product portfolio — including business banking expansion, new money services, and future consumer financial products — with the controls and operational readiness already in place.
  • Bring out the best in your people. Care deeply about the Gusties on your team. Help them do the best work of their careers, grow into bigger versions of themselves, and feel proud of building a risk and money function that protects Gusto's customers and the business at the same time.

Here's what we're looking for

  • 12+ years of industry experience leading financial services operations in banking, payments, money movement, fraud and risk, or related regulated domains — with demonstrated depth in the mechanics of how money moves, where it fails, and how regulated institutions respond.
  • 7+ years as a departmental leader running large, multi-disciplinary financial services operations teams — with experience managing through senior direct reports across distinct operational functions.
  • Deep expertise in banking and money movement operations — including Reg E dispute processing, BSA/AML operational response, ACH and real-time payments risk, sponsor bank operational requirements, and the controls infrastructure that makes regulated money movement auditable.
  • Hands-on background in fraud and payment risk — experience building or leading fraud operations that make real-time decisioning calls with material financial consequences, including payment risk scoring, account takeover response, and fund recovery operations.

descriptionHtml:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the role: 

The Senior Compensation Manager is a core member of Gusto's People team, responsible for building and scaling the compensation programs that help us attract, retain, and reward top talent. This role exists to bring rigor, fairness, and strategic clarity to how Gusto thinks about pay — operating at the intersection of data, policy, and people.

Operating with a systems-first, AI-native mindset, the Senior Compensation Manager uses automation, scalable workflows, and well-designed tooling to improve decision quality, ensure compliance, and reduce reliance on manual, one-off analysis. This role partners closely with HR Business Partners, Finance, Legal, and business leaders to ensure our compensation programs are grounded in market reality and aligned to our values.

Success in this role is measured by the quality and fairness of compensation decisions, the scalability and reliability of our programs, and the degree to which the organization can operate with confidence — without constant intervention or heroics.

Gusto's compensation function, built on first-principles thinking, is at an inflection point — scaling from early foundations to a mature, high-trust operation. You'll have real ownership to shape how we design and deliver compensation as the company grows.

Here's what you'll do day to day:

  • Develop, implement, and communicate Gusto's compensation programs, policies, and procedures, ensuring internal equity, external competitiveness, and alignment with business strategy.
  • Partner with and influence key stakeholders — including HRBPs, Finance, and senior leadership — to translate compensation philosophy into clear, actionable programs.
  • Lead annual compensation cycles (merit, equity refresh, benchmarking) and own the end-to-end process from data collection through communication.
  • Perform market analyses and compensation studies using survey data (e.g., Radford/Aon, Mercer, Pave) to recommend pay ranges, job levels, and offer positioning.
  • Use AI tools and automation thoughtfully to accelerate analysis, synthesize benchmarking data, and reduce planning and reporting load — while maintaining sound judgment around data quality and decision guardrails.
  • Design and maintain scalable compensation workflows and tooling — automating recurring analyses, audit processes, and reporting so programs run reliably without manual intervention.
  • Build and maintain compensation dashboards and data visualizations that give leaders real-time insight into pay equity, market positioning, and budget utilization.
  • Craft competitive, compelling offers to attract top-tier talent, and build playbooks to help recruiters and HRBPs communicate Gusto's total rewards story.
  • Ensure ongoing compliance with federal, state, and local pay regulations — including pay transparency laws, FLSA classification standards, and emerging pay equity requirements — and proactively flag legislative changes.
  • Partner with People Operations to integrate and optimize HRIS and compensation tools, ensuring data accuracy and system scalability as the company grows.

Here's what we're looking for:

  • 12+ years of experience in Compensation, Total Rewards, People Operations, or a related analytical function — ideally in a high-growth technology environment.
  • AI fluency: hands-on experience using AI tools or automation to accelerate analysis or synthesis, paired with strong judgment around trust and validation.
  • Hands-on experience running compensation cycles (merit, equity, benchmarking) and building scalable programs from early-stage to maturity.
  • Survey benchmarking fluency: direct experience with Radford/Aon, Mercer, Pave, or comparable compensation survey tools and methodologies.
  • Systems-first orientation: experience building durable workflows, automating reports, or designing operating mechanisms that reduce recurring manual work.

This is a high-visibility role at the intersection of performance marketing, channel experimentation, and AI-powered workflow design. You will own execution and day-to-day strategy for paid social and new channel tests, working within Gusto's demand generation framework, with clear accountability to pipeline and revenue targets.

About the Team

As a member of Gusto’s Demand Generation team, you will be embedded specifically within Paid Acquisition, a focused group responsible for driving awareness and pipeline through paid media. We hold ourselves to a high standard, move fast, and genuinely believe that being AI-native is part of what it means to do this job well today.

  • Apply and help refine Gusto's paid acquisition measurement framework, including attribution philosophy and budget allocation principles, in partnership with the broader marketing team.
  • Lead creative strategy and testing at scale: briefing creative studios and agencies, structuring meaningful experiments, interpreting complex data sets to drive actionable insights, and building a clear learning roadmap.

  • Partner with Web Marketing to align on landing page strategy, message match, and post-click conversion, because paid social performance doesn't end at the click.
  • Align with the Brand and Influencer team to run the organic-to-paid feedback loop — turning proven organic and influencer content into paid scale, and feeding results back to sharpen what earns that investment next.
  • Collaborate with Engineering to launch new pixels and tracking, troubleshoot platform-side issues, and QA implementations — keeping measurement reliable as tracking needs evolve.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Integrated Marketing, Product Marketing, Sales, Communications, and Web to align paid social with integrated campaigns and earned media moments, and bring performance data back upstream to influence creative production and asset strategy.

  • 7+ years of performance marketing experience at a B2B SaaS, performance marketing agency, or high-growth consumer organization, with deep expertise in paid social and a track record of testing and scaling new channels.

Payment Operations sits within Gusto's Money team, a cross-functional group spanning Engineering, Product, and Operations that powers money movement across Gusto's growing product surface: core payroll, contractor payments, international money movement, and new business offerings like PEO.

As a Payment Operations Analyst, you'll own specific end-to-end payment workflows, resolve exceptions that require real judgment, and help make our systems more reliable and efficient over time. Gusto's payment surface area is expanding — and this team is at the center of that growth.

This is a role for someone who can shift from investigating a single misfired transaction to coordinating a response on a payment outage affecting thousands — and bring the same rigor to both.   • Connect the dots across rails, partners, reconciliation, compliance, and customer experience. When an issue surfaces, you understand how it ripples — and you bring that perspective to cross-functional conversations.

Operating across native iOS and Android environments, you will leverage modern declarative frameworks (SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose), a shared GraphQL API layer, and AI-native workflows to deliver seamless end-to-end features. Your work will focus on improving financial tools for everyday employees, helping them reduce financial stress, build healthy money habits, and gain greater control over their paychecks. You will collaborate with a talented cross-functional team, contributing technical leadership throughout the product development lifecycle—from ideation and architecture to release and long-term scaling.

About the Team:

The Consumer Money team is on a mission to help employees achieve financial peace of mind by bridging employment and personal finances. The team's product suite gives workers complete control over their money—including on-demand pay, high-yield cash accounts, and automated savings—all anchored to the paycheck relationship Gusto uniquely powers.

Operating as one of the fastest-growing engines within Gusto Money, the team builds at a fast, startup-like pace. Beyond scaling core worker-facing products, the team is actively incubating 0-to-1 foundational technologies to power Gusto’s broader financial platform vision. Handling people’s livelihoods in a regulated banking space requires combining rapid innovation with deep technical rigor, system reliability, and an uncompromised focus on user experience. This role represents a high-impact opportunity to help shape the future of personal and platform finance at Gusto.

  • Help drive the product development process from concept to launch, ensuring high standards of technical rigor, system performance, and mobile security in a regulated banking domain
  • Adopt and maximize the latest best practices for using AI technologies (e.g. Claude) to accelerate cross-platform feature translation, raise code quality, and optimize team velocity

  • 8+ years of professional mobile software development experience with deep expertise in at least one primary native stack (Swift/iOS or Kotlin/Android)
  • Willingness and desire to flex across both mobile platforms (iOS and Android), building natively using SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose backed by shared API contracts and AI translation workflows
  • Deep understanding of modern declarative UI paradigms (SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose), reactive state management, and unidirectional data flow
  • A product-first mindset with a willingness and aptitude to flex across both iOS and Android using strong mobile fundamentals and AI translation workflows
  • Maximizes the use of AI tooling while guiding the team in adopting modern AI practices
  • Experience leading multi-quarter technical initiatives from scoping and architecture to launch and post-release monitoring
  • Experience working with strongly typed API layers (GraphQL) and managing offline caching, state synchronization, and complex mobile data contracts
  • Comfortable dealing with ambiguity, quick iteration cycles, and helping facilitate informed technical tradeoffs
  • An aptitude and interest in bringing clarity and simplicity to complex and ambiguous problems

  • Experience in the Fintech or banking industry building high-reliability, zero-defect mobile applications
  • Familiarity with mobile infrastructure, including CI/CD pipelines, automated testing environments, and build & release systems
  • Experience with MVVM or modern unidirectional architecture patterns

About the Role:

We're looking for a builder to help construct a world class Growth organization. This is an opinionated leader that is motivated by creating big picture vision and digging into where the biggest opportunities are, sizing them, and building the systems, rigor, and connective tissue that let Growth and GTM operate cohesively. This is a member of Gusto's Insights & Operations (I&O) team — our internal Strategy/BizOps function — embedded against Growth, partnering closely with our Head of Growth and our CRO-side GTM leadership.

This role is intentionally IC-first. You'll start by going deep on the highest-leverage problems in Growth, build a point of view grounded in data, and drive it to outcome. As trust and scope grow, this role is expected to expand — most likely into owning the operating bridge between Growth and our broader go-to-market organization, and potentially into building and leading a small team.

About the Team:

Gusto's Growth organization is on an ambitious trajectory: we're building toward a much more self-serve-led motion, and the opportunity ahead is significant. As Growth scales, we have a chance to be much more intentional about how it connects to Product and to our go-to-market teams (sales, demand gen, expansion sales, pricing, etc) — building a shared, prioritized roadmap and clear visibility into dependencies from the ground up, rather than retrofitting it later.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Identify and size the highest-leverage opportunities for Growth: go from a fuzzy problem to a clear-eyed analysis of the opportunity, a recommendation on whether to pursue it, and a plan if the answer is yes.
  • Anchor on problems, not headcount: dig into what's actually slowing the Growth organization down, define how to build a best in class engine, size the opportunity, and decide what's worth solving before proposing who or what is needed — not the reverse.
  • Build the operating rhythm for Growth and drive execution against it: planning cycles, prioritization, and a shared, prioritized roadmap that makes trade-offs and dependencies visible across Growth R&D, Product R&D, and GTM.
  • Bring real analytical rigor to how Growth invests — attribution, LTV, and testing/experimentation discipline — so decisions about where to deploy resources are tied clearly to business impact.
  • Close the gap between Growth R&D and go-to-market: build the mechanisms (shared roadmap, dependency tracking, decision forums) that let both orgs operate as one team working toward the same number, rather than two orgs trading requests.
  • Design an operating system anchored in technology vs. humans: build the muscle and mechanisms the Growth org can through automation, and hand off ownership once a system is running
  • Act as a trusted advisor to Growth leadership: pressure-test strategy, surface risks and blind spots early, and bring an opinionated point of view, not just facilitation.
  • Use AI as a default, not an add-on: build reusable, AI-powered workflows for planning, synthesis, and reporting so manual coordination is the exception, not the norm.
  • Spot when a team is optimizing for the wrong thing: recognize when more effort against the current approach won't get us where we need to go, and push teams toward a fundamentally different path rather than a marginal improvement.
  • Raise the bar for how I&O operates, not just how Growth operates: share what's working, question what isn't, and help the broader I&O team build a stronger, more consistent craft.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 15+ years in operations, business operations, or strategy & ops at a high-growth technology company. This must include time spent building a growth function from an earlier, less mature stage.
  • Direct experience with the discipline behind growth decision-making: attribution and LTV modeling, testing and experimentation, and translating marketing/growth spend into demonstrable business impact.
  • A track record of working at the intersection of growth and go-to-market (or product and sales) — connecting teams with different incentives around a shared goal.
  • A strong point of view on how operations should scale: knowing when a problem needs a dedicated system vs. when it needs reprioritization, and resisting the urge to grow headcount by default.
  • Comfort starting as an individual contributor — going deep on one problem set before taking on broader scope — balanced with a demonstrated ability to build and lead teams when the moment calls for it.
  • Exceptional organizational skills, able to manage multiple senior stakeholders and competing priorities in a fast-moving environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication — able to tailor for executive audiences and drive alignment on hard, ambiguous trade-offs.
  • Financial acumen: comfortable managing financial tracking and reporting across a complex org
  • Low ego and a bias toward collaboration: someone who works well across teams that all want the same outcome but don't yet have the bridges to get there together.
  • Deep empathy and enthusiasm for small business customers, and excitement about joining a company still very much in its building phase.

About you

  • You're drawn to ambiguity, not intimidated by it — you'd rather build the map than wait for someone to hand you one.
  • You have a point of view and you share it — you'd rather say the harder, more useful thing than stay neutral to keep the peace.
  • You're energized by change and by building something new, even when it means occasionally undoing your own work to get it right.
  • You default to using AI to move faster and think bigger, and you save your own time and judgment for the calls only a person can make.

title: Recruiting Operations and Transformation Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role

We're looking for a strategic and execution-oriented Lead, Recruiting Process Transformation to lead the evolution of our recruiting ecosystem. This leader will identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate Recruiting processes while ensuring operational excellence across our Recruiting Operations and Candidate Experience teams.

Reporting into the People Operations, Services & Technology (POST) organization, this role sits at the intersection of strategy, technology, and operations. You'll partner across Recruiting, People Tech, Legal, and business leaders to redesign how hiring gets done — from requisition to offer to onboarding handoff — creating scalable experiences for candidates, hiring teams, and Recruiting partners.

In addition to leading enterprise process transformation initiatives for recruiting, you'll oversee the teams responsible for executing our core Recruiting workflows, including Recruiting Operations and Candidate Experience.

What You'll Do

Lead Recruiting Process Transformation

  • Develop and execute a multi-year strategy for transforming recruiting processes.
  • Analyze end-to-end candidate and hiring lifecycle workflows; from requisition intake through offer and onboarding handoff; to identify friction, inefficiencies, redundancies, and opportunities for simplification.
  • Redesign processes using Lean, service design, and automation principles.
  • Consult with technical partners to understand how tooling, AI, and agentic solutions (e.g., InviteOS) can support improved recruiting efficiency.
  • Build business cases that quantify operational impact, candidate/hiring team experience improvements, and ROI.
  • Prioritize transformation initiatives based on organizational impact, scalability, and strategic objectives.
  • Partner with Recruiting leadership to define, track, and report on recruiting metrics
  • Diagnose root causes behind unmet KPIs and drive them to resolution, launching transformation initiatives where applicable.

Drive Technology-Enabled Improvements

  • Partner closely with People Technology to implement technology solutions that improve recruiting operational efficiency, including AI-native recruiting platforms such as InviteOS, our custom recruiting tool.
  • Evaluate opportunities to leverage workflow automation, AI, integrations, self-service capabilities, and system enhancements (Greenhouse, sourcing tools, scheduling tools) to drive prioritization for recruiting technology.
  • Ensure process design and technology decisions work together to create sustainable solutions.
  • Balance configuration, workflow redesign, and policy changes to achieve desired outcomes.

Lead Operational Excellence

Provide leadership for:

Recruiter Operations

  • Own transformation of core recruiting workflows, requisition management, and interview/offer processing.
  • Ensure operational accuracy, compliance, and service level achievement across the hiring pipeline.
  • Continuously improve throughput, quality, and controls across sourcing-to-offer stages.

Candidate Experience

  • Lead the team responsible for candidate-facing support and experience across the hiring journey.
  • Partner with People Tech to evaluate and deploy modern technology solutions or replace current solutions where needed.
  • Improve service delivery through knowledge management, self-service, case management optimization, and interview/scheduling process improvements.
  • Develop candidate experience metrics and continuously improve satisfaction and time-to-fill outcomes.

Establish Operational Governance

  • Define operational standards, process ownership, documentation, and governance across Recruiting operations.
  • Create KPI dashboards measuring efficiency, quality, service levels, cycle times, automation adoption, and candidate experience.
  • Build mechanisms to continuously identify improvement opportunities through operational data (e.g., Greenhouse reporting, PHC-style ticket analysis) and candidate/hiring manager feedback.

Lead and Develop Teams

  • Lead and coach managers and individual contributors across Recruiting Operations and Candidate Experience.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, operational excellence, and candidate-centric thinking.
  • Build organizational capability in process improvement methodologies and change management.

Partner Across the Business

  • Influence senior stakeholders across Recruiting leadership, People Tech, Finance, IT, Security, and Legal.
  • Translate business hiring priorities into operational improvements.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives requiring alignment across multiple organizations.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in Recruiting Operations, Talent Acquisition Operations, Business Operations, Process Excellence, Consulting, or related fields.
  • 5+ years leading managers and operational teams.
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise-scale process transformation initiatives.
  • Experience managing recruiting operations, candidate experience/support, or similar service organizations.
  • Strong understanding of recruiting technology ecosystems (Greenhouse or comparable ATS, sourcing tools, scheduling/case management platforms).
  • Experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, business process management, or operational excellence methodologies.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to use operational metrics (time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, candidate satisfaction) to drive decisions.
  • Proven ability to influence senior leaders without direct authority.
  • Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in high-growth technology companies.
  • Experience implementing recruiting technology or enterprise workflow platforms.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled recruiting automation and candidate support technologies.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent operational excellence training.
  • Experience leading organizational change and large cross-functional programs.

Success in This Role

Within your first year, you will have:

  • Established a transformation roadmap for Recruiting operations.
  • Identified and delivered measurable improvements in key candidate and hiring lifecycle processes.
  • Reduced manual work through workflow redesign and automation.

About the Role

This is your chance to own one of the most technical, horizontal levers in GTM planning: building the scalable models and infrastructure that enable every route to market to grow efficiently. As Senior Sales Operations Analyst, you’ll partner with GTM leaders, Finance, Revenue Operations, and GTM Ops to develop and execute segmentation, book-of-business design, quota setting, and capacity planning. You’ll turn GTM strategy into concrete, automated models that determine how customers are segmented, how reps are staffed, and what they are held accountable for.

This role takes an end-to-end, platform-minded view across GTM motions, not just a single sales team. You’ll identify where manual work, fragmented logic, or inconsistent processes limit scale and build durable planning infrastructure that drives revenue outcomes as the business evolves. You’ll own the outcome: balanced books, defensible quotas tied to capacity, and scalable models that hold up under scrutiny.

About the Team

You'll sit within GTM Operations, working as the dedicated segmentation, book-of-business, and capacity planning owner for our Direct, Expansion, and Benefits sales teams. We think of ourselves as builders and problem solvers: we turn ambiguous planning questions into scalable, defensible models, and we hold the line on rigor even when the business is moving fast and priorities compete.

You'll work in close partnership with each organization's GTM leaders and their dedicated GTM Ops partners, leaning on their operational and business context, while you own building, defending, and maintaining the segmentation, book, quota, and headcount models that everyone plans against.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day

Segmentation & Book of Business

  • Own the design and ongoing maintenance of customer/account segmentation for Direct, Expansion, and Benefits sales, translating org-level segmentation strategy into concrete, rules-based models these teams can operate against.
  • Build and maintain balanced books of business across reps and teams, accounting for account potential, workload, geography, and product mix; own rebalancing when the business shifts (new hires, departures, territory changes, book splits).
  • Set and maintain clear, documented rules for account assignment, routing, and reclassification, and serve as the ruling authority when edge cases or disputes come up.
  • Partner with Sales, GTM Ops, and Systems & Tooling to ensure segmentation and book structures are reflected accurately in Salesforce and downstream systems.

Quota Setting

  • Own the end-to-end quota-setting process for Direct, Expansion, and Benefits: translating top-down revenue targets into bottoms-up, capacity-based quotas by rep, team, and segment.
  • Build and maintain the quota models and methodology, ensuring quotas are defensible, equitable across territories/books, and tightly tied to book-of-business design and headcount capacity.
  • Partner with RTM leaders, Finance, and Sales Compensation to align quotas with comp plans, revenue targets, and business priorities each planning cycle.
  • Own quota administration through the cycle: true-ups for territory or book changes, new-hire ramp adjustments, and mid-cycle corrections.

Headcount & Capacity Planning

  • Partner with GTM Ops & Finance on capacity planning for Direct, Expansion, and Benefits: modeling the headcount needed to cover segmented books and hit revenue targets, and identifying where the org is over- or under-staffed relative to opportunity.
  • Build the headcount models that inform hiring plans, partnering with RTM leaders and Finance on timing, sequencing, and prioritization of new roles.
  • Continuously monitor capacity against actual book size, productivity, and attrition, flagging gaps or imbalances before they become a problem.
  • Own scenario planning for headcount and territory changes (reorgs, new segments, M&A, product launches), modeling the impact before decisions are made.

Cross-functional Partnership & Communication

  • Partner closely with RTM leaders and their GTM Ops partners across Direct, Expansion, and Benefits to ensure segmentation, book, quota, and capacity decisions reflect real operational context, while retaining ownership of the outcome and the execution.
  • Work with GTM Ops, Finance, and Sales Compensation to stay aligned with org-wide segmentation frameworks, revenue targets, and comp design.
  • Communicate clearly and proactively with sales leadership on plan status, tradeoffs, and risk: you're the trusted authority on "how the books, quotas, and headcount are built and why."
  • Document methodology and decisions so segmentation, quota, and capacity models are transparent, auditable, and repeatable across planning cycles.

Here's what we're looking for

  • 5+ years in Sales Ops, RevOps, or a similar analytical GTM role, with direct, hands-on experience owning segmentation, territory/book design, quota setting, or headcount/capacity planning; ideally in a fast-paced SaaS or fintech environment.
  • Proven ability to own outcomes and execution, not just analysis or recommendations: you're comfortable being the accountable owner when a quota, book, or headcount plan is challenged.
  • Strong sales process & tooling proficiency: you can build and audit account assignment/routing logic, manage territory and book structures, and build reporting that leaders trust.
  • Analytical depth; comfortable building and defending quantitative models (quota, capacity, segmentation) under time pressure.
  • Experience running planning processes on a recurring cadence (annual/quarterly quota setting, ongoing book rebalancing, headcount reviews) across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; you can defend a model's methodology to GTM leaders and senior sales leadership, and hold your ground when a decision is unpopular but correct.
  • A first-principles problem solver who can build a defensible model from ambiguous inputs and translate org-level strategy into concrete, rules-based execution.
  • A strong cross-functional partner, able to work closely with GTM leaders and GTM Ops peers without ceding ownership of the outcome.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience owning segmentation, book-of-business, or quota/capacity planning across multiple sales organizations or motions simultaneously (e.g., new business, expansion, and a distinct product line).
  • Experience in payroll, HR tech, benefits, or SMB SaaS go-to-market motions.
  • Experience partnering with Sales Compensation and Finance on quota-to-comp alignment.
  • Experience designing or improving account assignment/routing automation (e.g., lead-routing tools, rules engines).

descriptionHtml:
About Gusto

About the Role:

At Gusto, the rapid evolution of work requires a dynamic, agile capability infrastructure. As artificial intelligence transforms technical and leadership skills quarter to quarter, our team members need to upskill and adapt seamlessly. To meet this demand, we are building an innovative, agile capability model and tech-forward development ecosystem that delivers blended learning experiences and modular enablement directly in the flow of work.

We are seeking a talent product leader to spearhead the design and development of our enterprise capability framework across both individual contributor and leadership tracks. In this high-impact, strategic role, you will architect the foundational engine for our Talent Development function. Beyond defining the capability model, you will manage the full product lifecycle of our learning solutions—from user discovery and MVP prototyping to shipping, scaling, and maintaining high-impact learning products. You will define the taxonomy that powers modular content, partner with learning technology teams to set system integration requirements, and shape high-potential and executive leadership criteria.

As a talent development leader, you will translate validated capability data into scalable standards, establishing a single source of truth across the organization. You will leverage strong cross-functional judgment, partnering directly with HR business partners and executive leaders to diagnose capability gaps, prioritize strategic investments, and build future-proof learning solutions. If you are a technical instructional designer or learning architect passionate about AI-forward enablement, modular learning design, and scaling capability infrastructure, this role offers a unique opportunity to drive transformation.

About the Team:

The Talent Development team acts as a strategic partner to the business, diagnosing capability needs and architecting systems that empower employees to build their best careers. We move beyond traditional programs to design the organizational conditions that create clarity, connection, and commitment. By partnering with HR and business leaders, we align learning directly to organizational strategy, using AI and design to embed development into the flow of work.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Agile Capability Framework & Taxonomy: Define the product roadmap for our capability framework, managing it as a live product that evolves based on user needs, performance data, and business strategy across individual contributor and leadership tracks, explicitly embedding AI-native competencies.
  • Collaborative Learning Experience Design & Agile Delivery: Partner directly with content designers to co-create, build, and ship blended learning experiences, using iterative development cycles to continuously improve and scale solutions in response to evolving business needs.
  • Modular Enablement Strategy: Establish the strategic vision for core enablement programs using a hub-and-spoke model, collaborating with curriculum designers and content leads to scale blended learning experiences.
  • Modular Architecture & Content Governance: Own the architectural design for modular content and automated governance, establishing standards for chunking, tagging, and dynamically updating learning objects as source material or business needs evolve.
  • Cross-Functional Data Validation & Prioritization: Partner closely with HR business partners and executive stakeholders to analyze skill data, validate capabilities, and align learning investments with core business goals.
  • Tech-Forward & Workflow Integration: Collaborate with People Technology teams to write functional and technical requirements for the capability engine, productizing learning experiences natively within HR tech platforms and daily workflows.
  • Enterprise Advisory & Capability Translation: Partner directly with executive and business leaders across the enterprise to proactively diagnose emerging capability needs, translating complex operational priorities into clear, accessible training and actionable guidance.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • Typically 8+ years of progressive experience in Talent Development, Learning Architecture, Technical Instructional Design, or Organizational Design, with a track record of building foundational programs from scratch.

  • Support compliance with federal, state, and local pay regulations, including pay transparency postings, FLSA classification reviews, and annual survey submissions.
  • Document and improve compensation processes so that the work is repeatable, auditable, and not dependent on any one person's memory.

About the Role

This is a highly customer-facing role at the intersection of engineering, solution architecture, agentic AI, and customer delivery. You will work directly with stakeholders and own the technical discovery for our ongoing opportunities end to end. Once a deal is qualified, you scope, build, embed with the client, and build it yourself, code that holds up against real tax and jurisdiction data, not a prototype you clean up later. What you ship only counts once the client is paying for it, it's live, and it's measurably cutting the manual work they used to do by hand, hours saved, tickets deflected, risk reduced. You should be comfortable speaking with both technical and executive stakeholders, moving quickly from problem discovery to prototype, and turning complex workflows into production-ready agents and multi-agent systems.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day

  • Scope & Qualify: Give Sales a technical feasibility read early on ambiguous Enterprise opportunities, then own scoping the compliance challenge once the deal is sales-qualified.
  • Define the Problem: Own requirements gathering on complex, ambiguous opportunities, scoping the problem clearly enough for Sales, Product, and Engineering to align on it.
  • Prove It First: Build a working proof-of-concept of the proposed agent when a deal needs to see feasibility before committing to the full build, tailored from a hands-on integration engineer to a VP of Payroll Tax.
  • Make the Business Case: Translate every deployment into the business case that justifies the subscription: hours saved, risk reduced, compliance simplified.
  • Own the Build: Embed with clients and write the code yourself, work that runs their compliance decisions instead of just connecting to them. There's no fixed method yet, you figure out what each engagement needs and build it.
  • Clear the Blockers: Diagnose and fix the data issues, jurisdiction mapping, tax ID reconciliation, that stand between a client and production.
  • Bridge the Gap: Keep technical teams and business stakeholders aligned as requirements evolve mid-engagement, so scope changes don't blindside either side.
  • Own the Handoff: Deliver the build and a runbook Client Success runs solo without the need to loop back the FDE.
  • Close the Loop: Feed structured signal from both the sales motion and the build motion back into product and go-to-market strategy, including infrastructure gaps.
  • Create Implementation Playbooks: solution patterns, demo flows, and deployment documentation that make future deployments faster.

Here's what we're looking for

  • Demonstrated 5+ years of hands-on experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, AI Engineer, Implementation Engineer, Solutions Architect, Technical Consultant, or similar.
  • Proven track record of shipping production systems in ambiguous, client-facing environments, with demonstrable evidence of:
    • REST APIs, webhooks, event-driven systems, auth patterns, data modeling, idempotency, and failure modes, not just happy-path builds
    • Building production systems in highly regulated categories, payroll, tax, or compliance fluency deep enough to run a conversation with a client's compliance team without a translator
    • Agentic workflows beyond prototypes: MCP or function-calling patterns, evaluation and reliability practices
  • Deep technical discovery skills with the ability to navigate a high degree of ambiguity
  • Ability to scope a technical solution from an ambiguous opportunity, build the business case that justifies a subscription, and ship a pattern the next engagement can reuse
  • Proven ability to present to and influence a range of audiences, from individual engineers to executive sponsors
  • Entrepreneurial, passionate about our mission, and deep empathy for the clients whose compliance work you're automating
  • Bonus points for experience with a specific HR/payroll platform's integration surface, enterprise procurement or security review processes, or MEDDPICC-style deal frameworks

Who Thrives Here

Builders who can sit with a customer, understand the real problem, quickly build an agentic solution, and present it clearly enough that the customer immediately sees the value.

You’ll thrive here if you are technical, customer-facing, fast-moving, and independent. You prototype and debug rather than only coordinate. You take responsibility for the customer outcome, communicate proactively, flag risks early, and follow through. You are comfortable being the technical adult in the room, whether you’re speaking with a customer’s architect, operations lead, engineering team, or VP of Payroll.

We’re looking for someone low-ego, collaborative, sharp, and highly accountable - someone who can build trust with customers while also building real technical solutions.

Our total cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $88,000-140,000 in Scottsdale, $95,000-150,000 in Denver, and $115,000-181,000 in New York & San Francisco Bay Area. Stock equity is additional. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

About the Role:

Gusto is building its own P&C insurance agency — moving from a third-party referral model to a first-party, payroll-integrated experience that protects small businesses as they grow. We have policies in force and a growing book of business. What we don't yet have is a licensed account manager inside the company servicing it. You'll be our first, and the foundation of the service function: owning daily servicing of the book, running the proactive outreach that keeps clients correctly covered, and turning every recurring case into a product spec so the next hundred don't need a human.

About the Team:

The Business Insurance team is building Gusto's P&C insurance agency from the ground up, across core small commercial lines including Workers' Compensation. We partner closely with carrier counterparts and work hand-in-hand with product, engineering, design, data, sales, and licensed insurance professionals to ship a quote, bind, and service experience that's fast, accurate, and easy to manage over time. The team is small, cross-functional, and highly execution-oriented — ideal for someone who thrives in ambiguity and wants to build durable operations in a zero-to-one environment.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Own daily servicing of the assigned book: endorsements, certificates of insurance, coverage questions, premium audits, billing disputes, cancellations, reinstatements, and renewals.
  • Accountable for outcomes connected to Business Insurance customers. 
  • Serve as the liaison between insureds, carriers, and our licensed producers — explaining coverage, exclusions, and exposures in plain language.
  • Run proactive outreach using payroll data a traditional agency doesn't have: catching FEIN mismatches, new-state hires, and class code drift before they become coverage gaps.
  • Work the pending cancellation and non-pay queue — find out what's actually driving each cancellation, fix what's fixable, and secure reinstatement or replacement coverage.
  • Handle claims intake and status reporting, and coordinate hand-offs to the carrier's adjusting team.
  • Document every recurring case as a product spec, partnering with product and engineering to automate certificate generation, endorsement submission, and intake triage — using AI tools daily for drafting, summarization, and triage.
  • Write the SOPs, escalation paths, and service standards for the team

    • 550,000 new businesses are created each year in the US (1) 

What Product Management is like at Gusto:

  • Our Product team is lean, which means you’ll have a high degree of impact and ownership. We believe in smaller, empowered teams that move quickly with less overhead. You’ll move fast by pairing sharp product judgment with fluency in AI tools, automating what slows teams down and amplifying what makes them creative and high-performing. 
  • We’re boundaryless builders. Lines between roles are intentionally blurred, and our PMs do whatever it takes to deliver outcomes. You’ll prototype, automate, design, and ship, using AI as your co-builder to turn problems into durable solutions that deliver customer value with urgency and care.
  • We’re here to serve small and medium businesses. Gusto has a strong mission-driven culture, and we care deeply about lifting up these business owners, building technology for an AI-first world that gives them the superpowers to run and grow their businesses with confidence.
  • We’re comfortable with change. Our environment moves fast, and PMs here thrive in ambiguity, blending curiosity, experimentation, and AI-native craft to shape how products (and work itself) are built at Gusto.

About the Team:

HR Experiences (HRX) builds the products that help small businesses hire, onboard, develop, and stay compliant: hiring and I-9s, performance, handbooks, training, labor law posters, and the tools our HR Partners use to serve their clients. Most of our customers are a department of one, an owner or office manager making consequential people decisions with no HR team to check their work.

Today we serve those customers mostly through software built in the GUI era: prescribed workflows and screens that customers have to learn, with human HR experts and advisory experiences for a growing set of them. For a meaningful segment, learning our workflows is not a must-have, and a GUI can never cover the long tail of needs that hundreds of thousands of businesses have. The opportunity ahead of us is to rebuild how HR gets delivered so that the product does the work and carries the judgment of an expert, and to make it AI-native from the start rather than a chat box bolted onto a GUI.

As Principal Product Manager, you'll be a senior individual contributor who owns the People Page experience and sets the experience direction for the HR Suite. You'll also own Training, which is where you'll build and learn quickly. You'll work hand in hand with the PM who owns the other verticals (Hiring, Onboarding, and Performance).

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Ownership: You will own the People Page experience and how it evolves: new entry points, interactive patterns, and the experience principles that apply to every vertical in the HR Suite (hiring, onboarding, performance, and training). Today those verticals are built as prescribed workflows, and the team is bringing them to market parity. Working with the PM who owns each vertical, you'll shape what they become when the product does the work for the customer, whether that is conversational, embedded, agentic, or something else entirely, and where a GUI still earns its place. Changes to Hiring, Onboarding, and Performance happen in partnership with the PM who owns them, once each vertical meets its parity floor, and verticals adopt your principles at a pace that PM sets. You'll also own the Training vertical end to end, using it to build, ship, and learn quickly before those patterns spread to the rest of the suite.
  • North Star: Move Gusto from the GUI era to an AI-native one. Our 550K businesses have needs that differ by state, size, industry, and risk tolerance, and we can't build a separate solution for each. Your goal is to deliver far more value across that long tail, so each customer gets what they specifically need: their context imported, a confident and compliant recommendation instead of a menu of options, and the work done for them. You'll prove it by moving adoption and outcomes, not feature counts.
  • Collaborate: You'll work closely with design, engineering, data, compliance, legal, product marketing, the PM who owns hiring, onboarding, and performance and the actions behind them, and our advisory teams (HR Partners and Ask an Expert), whose work shows where customers need judgment the product doesn't give today, to deliver outcomes no single team owns. Time with SMB HR operators is a regular part of the job.
  • Build, not just specify. Prototype with AI tools, work with engineering to take prototypes to production, instrument what matters, and iterate on what customers do. The goal is to build beyond today's GUIs once each vertical is at baseline, not to re-skin them. Conversation is one pattern among several, so you'll design the interactive patterns that fit each job. Where a conversational, embedded, or agentic model delivers more value than a prescribed workflow, you'll make that case and ship it.
  • Shape how the HR Suite shows up where customers already work, including Claude, ChatGPT, and other assistants, through MCP and integrations, in partnership with the PM who owns the action catalog, so a customer asking an AI assistant an HR question gets an answer grounded in their own Gusto data and can act on it without leaving the conversation.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 8+ years of direct Product Management experience, with a track record of owning a significant product surface end-to-end and shipping products that moved the business.
  • Real HR domain experience. You've lived these problems as a People/HR leader or founder who made these decisions firsthand, or you've built products in the HR, people, or compliance space. You know how an SMB HR operator thinks.
  • Fluency in AI product patterns: conversational and agentic interfaces, interaction patterns beyond chat, LLM capabilities and limits, and how to design experiences people can trust. You've shipped products where AI does the work rather than guiding a user through a workflow, or you're clearly hungry to. You build working prototypes yourself rather than waiting for a handoff.
  • A strong, opinionated point of view on where HR software is heading, and the judgment to tell a big swing from a distraction. You can set multi-year direction and still work through the details of a shipping feature, and you're comfortable getting a product to a competitive baseline first and building toward something bigger from there.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and complexity, especially where the hard problem is experience design and product formulation, and where compliance, privacy, and multi-tenant trust are design constraints to solve.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can make a sharp argument, rally a team around a direction, and bring skeptical stakeholders along.
  • A bias for customer truth over internal opinion, and the discipline to validate with real users.
  • Bonus: experience in HR, compliance, fintech, or another high-trust regulated domain; experience reimagining a mature, workflow-heavy product for AI, or converting an expert services motion into scaled software.

descriptionHtml:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

About the Role:

Gusto is seeking a Senior Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Investigations Analyst to support our Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) program. This is an individual contributor role within the EDD Investigations team, focused on conducting the most complex due diligence reviews to identify, assess, and mitigate regulatory, financial crime, and reputational risk.

In this role, you will independently perform in-depth EDD investigations for the highest-risk customers and most complex entity structures, using a combination of human judgment, open-source intelligence, and AI-enabled tools. You will provide specialized risk analysis to internal partners and make well-supported recommendations on onboarding, monitoring, and exit decisions, balancing regulatory obligations and customer experience.

EDD at Gusto presents unique and intellectually engaging challenges. Our platform supports hundreds of thousands of small businesses across diverse industries, ownership structures, and geographies, which means no two investigations look exactly alike. From onboarding through ongoing monitoring, you’ll work through nuanced risk profiles and layered entity structures that require rigor, sound judgment, and adaptability. This role is ideal for someone who can balance a high volume of reviews with deep, independent investigative work on complex matters, and who uses AI as a core part of how they work to improve both efficiency and quality.

About the Team:

The Enhanced Due Diligence Investigations team conducts thorough reviews of higher-risk customers and activities, from the point of onboarding through ongoing monitoring. The team performs Know Your Customer (KYC) reviews to verify that new customers are legitimate businesses, and evaluates ownership and control structures, source of wealth and funds, adverse media, sanctions exposure, and other risk indicators to ensure Gusto meets regulatory expectations and maintains platform integrity.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Independently conduct enhanced due diligence reviews for the highest-risk customers in accordance with internal procedures and regulatory expectations, including periodic and event-driven reviews
  • Perform in-depth open-source research and documentation analysis to assess adverse media, sanctions and PEP exposure, industry and geographic risk, source of funds and wealth, and beneficial ownership and control structures
  • Evaluate the most complex or multi-layered entities, synthesize findings into clear investigative summaries, and draft Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) when appropriate
  • Investigate and independently resolve EDD-related alerts involving sanctions exposure, adverse media, PEPs, marijuana-related businesses, or other elevated risk indicators, making sound, risk-based recommendations and escalating to EDD leadership where guidance is needed to resolve an issue
  • Independently perform KYC reviews during customer onboarding, verifying business legitimacy, identity, and beneficial ownership, and resolving complex or escalated cases, including those with opaque ownership structures, high-risk indicators, or conflicting information, with minimal guidance
  • Leverage AI-enabled tools to accelerate issue spotting, alert triage, research, and documentation, providing clear context and constraints through prompt refinement while maintaining human judgment and accountability
  • Critically review and edit AI-generated research or summaries to ensure accuracy, completeness, and regulatory soundness, applying Gusto's AI policies and data protection standards when handling sensitive information
  • Identify opportunities to improve investigative workflows, contribute to EDD desktop guides and training materials, and surface insights on emerging trends to support continuous program improvement
  • Mentor junior analysts on open-source research, beneficial ownership analysis, and risk documentation through case reviews and structured feedback

  • 5+ years of experience conducting enhanced due diligence, AML investigations, KYC, customer due diligence, or similarly deep investigative or research-driven work

About the Role:

We’re looking for a Head of Internal Controls to join Gusto’s Finance, BizOps & Strategy team. This leader will partner with accounting and technical leaders to build and scale a forward-thinking internal controls environment that supports Gusto’s growth and operational maturity.

As the Head of Internal Controls, you will lead Gusto’s controls program across business process controls and IT controls. The scope includes the proprietary and third-party systems supporting Gusto’s payroll, health benefits, retirement, and other financial products.

You will build the team, set the program’s strategy, and embed practical controls into how Gusto’s products, systems, and financial processes are designed and operated. You will also define what an AI-forward internal controls function can look like, both by applying AI to controls work and by establishing oversight of AI-enabled financial processes and software development.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on controls leader who has built or scaled an ICFR program and led experienced teams. They can engage collaboratively with accounting and technical leaders, understand proprietary systems and complex data flows, and translate risk into controls that support the business without creating unnecessary operational burden.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Build and lead Gusto’s internal controls function, bringing business process controls and IT controls together under a single program and developing the team needed to support both areas.
  • Own Gusto’s risk-based ICFR framework across financial processes and the systems and data that support them, including scoping, control design, documentation, testing, issue evaluation, and remediation.
  • Strengthen the control environment supporting Gusto’s complex operations, proprietary systems, and evolving products.
  • Partner early with Accounting, Finance, Product, Engineering, Data, Security, and Risk to build control and auditability into new products, systems, and processes without creating unnecessary manual work or disruption.
  • Set the vision for an AI-forward internal controls function, using AI and automation to rethink how risk is identified, evidence is evaluated, and controls are tested and monitored. Establish practical oversight for risks introduced by AI-enabled financial processes and software development.
  • Lead the relationship with external auditors, ensuring alignment on risk, scope, testing, evidence, and remediation.
  • Establish clear governance and accountability for internal controls, including training across Gusto and reporting to senior management and the Audit Committee on the program’s health and effectiveness.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in a Big 4 accounting firm, internal audit, or SOX compliance role program in a complex, scaling organization with professional certifications like CIA or CISA. 
  • 5+ years of people leadership experience, with a track record of hiring, coaching, and developing experienced controls professionals and distributing judgment and institutional knowledge across a team.
  • Deep knowledge of US GAAP, the COSO framework, and the requirements supporting management’s ICFR assessment and external auditor attestation.
  • Breadth across business process controls and IT controls, with depth in at least 1 discipline and the judgment to lead experienced specialists across both.
  • Experience in a technology-driven environment with proprietary applications, automated controls, complex data flows, high transaction volumes, and evolving products. Experience in fintech, payments, payroll, or financial services is preferred.

  • Build forecasting systems: Architect driver-based, ML-assisted forecasts for revenue, headcount, opex, and cash, combining statistical models with LLM workflows and benchmarking against human forecasts.

  • Measure impact: Report on cycle-time reduction, forecast accuracy, analyst capacity freed, and decision latency.

  • 10+ years in FP&A, corporate finance, finance systems, data science, or finance engineering, including 3+ years designing or leading AI/ML or advanced automation for finance

  • Proficiency in SQL and Python, a modern data stack (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, dbt), and BI tools
  • Experience with enterprise planning platforms and ERP/GL systems
  • Track record shipping production-grade solutions under SOX, data governance, and security review

  • Payroll, HR tech, fintech, or SaaS finance experience
  • Experience building internal tools with Engineering
  • Familiarity with MCP-style integrations and AI governance frameworks
  • CPA, CFA, or an advanced quantitative degree

Finance-fluent builder, systems thinker, rigorous about trust (evals, lineage, and human-in-the-loop as design requirements), pragmatic on build vs. buy, influencer and teacher, and outcome-driven.

Expert/Transformer level, expected to set AI standards for Finance. Advanced in LLM platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), agent frameworks and MCP, and Python/SQL; proficient in Snowflake/Databricks/dbt, planning platforms (Anaplan, Adaptive, Pigment), ERP/GL (NetSuite), and BI tools.

About the Role:

Franchise is one of Gusto's fastest-growing partner channels, and we are looking for a Partner Manager to own it. You will recruit and sign franchisors, and manage the partnerships once they are signed. When a franchisor becomes a Gusto partner, the franchisees in its network can access Gusto's payroll, benefits, and HR platform on partner terms. Franchisors are not traditional channel partners. They protect their brand, support independent owner-operators, and operate within legal limits on how they can endorse vendors. A signed agreement does not guarantee franchisee adoption. Your job is to make Gusto easy for a franchisor to approve and recommend, and to give franchisees a clear reason to choose us.   You will own the full partnership lifecycle for our managed partners (Silver through Platinum) and lead recruiting for our entry-level (Bronze) partners. You will work with a dedicated franchise Account Executive, the Mid-Market Sales team, Partner Marketing, Revenue Operations, and Legal. This role suits someone who enjoys building relationships with brand leaders, structuring agreements that work for both sides, and turning a growing partner portfolio into measurable customer growth.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

Recruit franchisor partners

  • Identify, qualify, and sign franchisors across emerging, growth-stage, and mature brands, with a focus on sectors such as health and wellness, children's businesses, and home services.
  • Run discovery on every new partner application and serve as the franchisor's main point of contact through onboarding.
  • Build outbound campaigns using prospect lists, partner referrals, franchise sales organizations, industry associations, and competitive displacement opportunities. Use AI and sales tools to research and reach decision-makers.
  • Represent Gusto at franchise industry events and trade shows, and follow up so those events turn into signed partners.

Structure and manage partnerships

  • Place each new partner in the right program tier based on their expected franchisee growth and engagement.
  • Structure and negotiate partner agreements, working with Legal and Revenue Operations on terms such as offers, revenue share, and co-marketing commitments.
  • Own the full lifecycle for managed (Silver–Platinum) partners: onboarding, joint planning, performance reviews, and renewals. Recruit and onboard Bronze partners, who are supported mainly through our partner management platform.
  • Agree on rules of engagement with each partner that set how Gusto may reach their franchisees, so outreach is welcome and the brand relationship is protected.

Drive franchisee adoption

  • Work with the franchise Account Executive and Mid-Market Sales on a shared list of target brands. Recruit the franchisor while sales works with that brand's franchisees.
  • Coordinate with Partner Marketing on co-branded assets, landing pages, webinars, and event outreach.
  • Work with franchisor headquarters teams, such as franchise support, onboarding, and training, to build franchisee awareness.
  • Explore integrations with the operating platforms franchisors use, together with our product and integrations teams.

Manage performance and operations

  • Meet or exceed monthly and annual goals by forecasting accurately and managing a pipeline of partners from first conversation to signature and beyond.
  • Use Salesforce and our partner management tools to track pipeline, contacts, agreements, and results. Report on key partner metrics to leadership.
  • Run regular performance reviews and manage contract commitments with each partner.
  • Be a thought partner to your team and to cross-functional colleagues, and help improve how we run the franchise program.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 5–7 years of relationship management, partnerships, business development, sales, or channel management experience. We prefer candidates with franchise industry experience, such as working with franchisors, franchisee associations, or franchise sales organizations.

  • A track record of building a pipeline through outbound prospecting and managing it from first conversation to signed agreement.
  • Comfort with data. You can set goals, forecast, and report on performance.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills, including with senior executives.
  • Experience with Salesforce is a plus. Experience with Outreach, partner management platforms, or fintech, HR, or payroll is also a plus.
  • AI fluency: you use AI tools in your daily work to research and prioritize prospects, draft and personalize outreach, analyze partner performance, and speed up routine tasks, and you apply your own judgment to the final result. You can describe how you build, refine, and check the AI workflows you use.
  • You are a quick learner who collaborates well. You are self-directed and resourceful, and you thrive in a fast-paced, changing environment where you think strategically and execute tactically.
