About the team 

The Security Operations team at Gusto plays a critical role in fortifying Gusto and our customers against sophisticated threats: phishing attacks, insider risks, data loss, and emerging attack techniques. Our distributed team across Eastern and Pacific time zones monitors, investigates, and responds to security events during business hours, with a lightweight rotation for rare after-hours escalation of critical incidents.

We're looking for a Security Operations analyst with 5+ years of experience to own and deliver security operations projects, take an active role in incident response, and raise the bar for how our team detects and responds to threats. You'll work across our multi-cloud environment (AWS, GCP, and others), build Python-based automation, and help govern the fastest-growing part of our attack surface: non-human identities and AI/agent connections. You'll be the directly responsible individual for medium-sized initiatives, work closely with senior analysts, and help mentor newer teammates.

Here's what you'll do

Own security operations projects end to end. Take medium-sized initiatives (typically 1-2 months, often spanning multiple teams) from problem definition through design, rollout, and measurement. Break down ambiguous goals into deliverables, set expectations with stakeholders, communicate progress and risks, and drive work to completion.

Lead and participate in incident response. Triage, investigate, and respond to security incidents across our cloud and corporate environments. Serve as a core responder, document root cause and remediation, write or contribute to post-mortems, and own the completion of post-mortem action items so lessons turn into lasting improvements.

Improve detection and monitoring. Monitor and triage alerts from tools like AWS GuardDuty/Security Hub/WAF, GCP Security Command Center, and our CSPM platform. Tune and improve detections, reduce noise, and recommend configuration and process improvements based on what you learn from investigations.

Build security operations automation. Write Python to extend our automation frameworks and SOAR playbooks, reducing manual work and improving response times. Own the quality, testing, and documentation of what you ship.

Threat hunting. Hunt for threats across our multi-cloud and corporate environments using threat intelligence and the team's playbooks, and turn findings into new detections or playbooks.

Non-human identity and agentic AI governance (roughly one-third of your time). Help govern machine identities, service accounts, and MCP/agent connections that now outnumber human accounts. Drive improvements such as expanding DLP/Nightfall policy coverage for AI and MCP-connected tools, attributing and cleaning up unowned cloud secrets and service accounts, and moving our MCP review process from reactive intake to proactive, risk-based governance.

AI-assisted security operations. Use AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Skills, MCP-connected tools) to work faster on querying, investigating, and drafting, and apply sound judgment about risks specific to AI tooling, such as prompt injection, data exfiltration through connected tools, and over-permissioned agents. Help set team norms for reviewing and validating AI-assisted work.

Collaborate and mentor. Partner with analyzing, IT, and product teams to support secure practices and communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Mentor newer teammates, share what you learn through documentation and knowledge sharing, and contribute to hiring by interviewing candidates.

Participate in the on-call rotation. This is a business-hours role with a lightweight on-call rotation for rare after-hours escalations, not a 24/7 pager rotation. You'll join the roster (currently about one week per month, shifting to roughly every 5-6 weeks as the team grows), respond to security incidents, and follow through on post-mortem action items afterward.

Here's what we're looking for

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, SOC analysis, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or serving as the primary owner of a project or initiative, including coordinating with other teams.
  • Hands-on experience responding to security incidents, including investigation, root cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.
  • Working knowledge of security monitoring, incident response, and vulnerability management.
  • Familiarity with core cloud security services across major providers (AWS, GCP, or similar) and cloud security fundamentals.
  • Comfortable working in Linux environments.
  • Proficiency in Python for scripting and automation.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise security tools (SIEM, EDR, SOAR, DLP). Deploying or architecting these tools from scratch is not expected at this level.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to communicate findings clearly and escalate appropriately.
  • Comfortable using AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Skills, MCP-connected tools), with a working understanding of AI-specific security risks (prompt injection, data exfiltration via connected tools/MCPs, over-permissioned agents) and how to mitigate them.
  • Familiarity with identity and access concepts (service accounts, API keys/tokens, OAuth) and curiosity about how AI agents and MCP-connected tools introduce new identity and access risk. Deep specialist experience is not expected at this level.
  • Willingness and ability to participate in a lightweight, business-hours-oriented on-call rotation.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with log analysis or digital forensics in cloud or on-premise environments.
  • Experience with incident response involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Experience writing or improving detections and playbooks.
  • Familiarity with common vulnerability classes and remediation approaches.
  • Exposure to CI/CD security concepts (e.g., dependency scanning tools like GitHub Dependabot).
  • Familiarity with common security frameworks (e.g., NIST, SOC 2).
  • Experience with identity and access management, non-human identity, secrets management, or MCP/agent architecture.
  • Experience mentoring or onboarding teammates.
  • Security certifications (e.g., Security+, GSEC) are a plus. Advanced certifications (CISSP, CISM, etc.) are not expected at this level.

In addition to providing expert advice, you’ll also work on defined projects for clients, starting with employee handbooks and compliance work. You’ll do well here if you get excited about compliance, enjoy moving quickly and balancing multiple stakeholders, and love to find new ways to leverage technology and AI to become more efficient and effective.

About the Team:

  • Answer HR questions clients submit via chat, using our AI tool to research, draft, and check responses, and own the accuracy of every answer you send.
  • Join client calls when a question needs a live conversation, and help clients work through it with clear, practical guidance.
  • Build and update employee handbooks for clients across multiple states, tailored to each client’s locations, headcount, and policy choices.
  • Deliver compliance projects, such as policy reviews, multi-state requirement checks, and required notices and postings.
  • Take on new project types as the team expands beyond handbooks and compliance, and help build the templates, playbooks, and processes that make them repeatable.
  • Recognize when a question needs more than a quick answer, whether that means routing to another Gusto team or recommending the client consult legal counsel, and hand it off with the right context.
  • Document your work in our systems of record, and flag patterns in the questions you see so we can improve our AI tool, client resources, and services.
  • Test new tools and processes and share constructive feedback and suggestions.
  • Step in to support our Gusto HR Partners team, who serve as fractional HR consultants for a set book of business, when additional capacity is needed.
  • Provide excellent customer service in every chat, call, and project.

Gusto is building its PEO sales org from the ground up, and we're looking for a quota-carrying seller to be one of the founding members of that team. This is a true ground-floor opportunity: you'll be among the first reps closing PEO business at Gusto, working directly with the Head of PEO Sales to prove out and scale the motion. You'll drive new PEO revenue by selling Gusto's co-employment solution to both net-new prospects and our existing base of 400,000+ customers — Gusto's single biggest competitive advantage over legacy PEOs. The market opportunity is real, the pace is fast, and the early sellers on this team will help define what "good" looks like.Use AI-powered workflows as a core part of how you sell: running assigned tools daily, surfacing friction and inefficiencies as you find them, and collaborating with your team to influence what gets built or improved next.  If you're excited to roll up your sleeves, lead by example, and architect something from scratch, let's talk.

About the Team:

You'll be an early individual contributor on Gusto's founding PEO sales team, reporting to the Head of PEO Sales. As one of the first sellers, you'll carry a personal book of business, run the full sales cycle end to end, and serve as a Subject Matter Expert who guides prospects through complex co-employment buying decisions. You'll partner closely with HR, benefits, and payroll counterparts to deliver a seamless customer experience, and you'll work alongside the Head of PEO to surface what's working in the field — feedback that directly shapes the playbook, tooling, and pipeline architecture as the org scales. Your biggest unfair advantage: Gusto's existing install base. Like the best scaled PEOs, a meaningful share of your pipeline will come from converting existing payroll customers to PEO — and you'll be one of the first to run that motion at scale.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Own the full sales cycle. Prospect, qualify, run discovery, demo, navigate complex buying groups, and close. This is a quota-carrying role for a seller who's comfortable owning a deal from first touch to signed agreement.
  • Sell across both motions. Close net-new prospects and convert existing Gusto payroll customers to PEO. You'll learn the distinct objections, value propositions, and rhythms of in-base selling vs. cold-start prospecting.
  • Serve as a PEO Subject Matter Expert. Guide prospects through co-employment, benefits, compliance, and the practical realities of moving onto a PEO. Build and maintain deep knowledge of PEO compliance, co-employment regulations, and applicable state and federal employment law.
  • Sell with selling-season fluency. Understand and plan around PEO's concentrated selling window (Sept–Dec, with the bulk of new business landing Jan 1). Build pipeline early and manage your funnel to hit those timelines.
  • Work the channel. Partner with broker, GA, and accountant referral sources to develop pipeline, and feed insights back on what's converting.
  • Manage your pipeline rigorously. Keep Salesforce clean and current, forecast accurately, and operate within the sales stages, routing, and reporting the team establishes.
  • Use AI to sell smarter. Bring genuine AI fluency to your daily workflow — leveraging AI tools for prospecting, call prep, follow-up, and forecast hygiene. We expect our sellers to be hands-on with AI and to share what's working with the broader team.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally. Work closely with Marketing, Product, and the broader Sales org to surface market signals, sharpen positioning, and improve the customer experience.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • PEO / HCM Sales Experience: 4+ years in a closing sales role, ideally in PEO, HCM, or benefits. Direct PEO selling experience is strongly preferred.
  • Quota Attainment: Consistent, demonstrable track record of meeting and exceeding individual sales targets.
  • Full-Cycle Ownership: Proven ability to own a deal end to end — prospecting, discovery, multi-stakeholder navigation, and close — in a consultative, complex sale.
  • Selling-Season Fluency: Familiarity with PEO's Jan 1 selling cycle (Sept–Dec pipeline build, renewal dynamics) is a strong plus and a key screen for PEO-specific experience vs. generic HCM.
  • Install-Base Conversion: Experience selling into or converting an existing customer base to a higher-tier or adjacent product is a plus.
  • Channel Familiarity: Understanding of broker, GA, and accountant referral channels in the PEO or benefits space.
  • Sales Acumen: Strong working knowledge of inbound and outbound sales methodologies in SMB SaaS or HCM/PEO environments.
  • Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across HR, Benefits, Product, and Marketing; excellent interpersonal skills.
  • AI Fluency: Proven, day-to-day experience integrating AI into how you work — across writing, research, prep, and summarization as a core part of your workflow, with a track record of giving clear, useful feedback that helps improve your tools and processes.
  • Technical Proficiency: Salesforce.com (SFDC) experience required; familiarity with HCM platforms and benefits administration tools preferred.

What You’ll Do

  • Architect & Execute GTM Strategy
    Lead go-to-market strategy and execution for business insurance, partnering with Growth, Product and Marketing to shape customer segmentation, pricing, and GTM motions that drive adoption and growth.
  • Turn Insights Into Action
    Synthesize market research, customer insights, usage data, and cross-functional input to identify opportunities and inform strategy. Translate strategy into actionable plans and ensure GTM execution lands with excellence.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Alignment & Accountability
    Work across Product, Sales, Marketing, Data Science, and Finance to agree on shared goals and coordinate execution. Bring structure, momentum, and accountability to complex initiatives. Build new ways of working by building net-new processes/systems that didn’t exist prior.
  • Make Growth Channels Self-Serve
    Define requirements and program parameters, work with the Growth team on what they build and how it runs, and make sure tools like in-app and AI levers are usable, scalable, and trackable for product marketers.
  • Own Performance & Optimization
    Define success metrics and track performance across initiatives. Drive regular reviews of GTM performance and lead iteration to improve outcomes over time.
  • Work AI-First
    Use AI tools to accelerate research, synthesize insights, and refine positioning and content with speed and precision.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • 8+ years of experience in marketing or product management and 3+ in product marketing
  • Track record of shaping GTM strategy in ambiguous yet highly ambitious environments: 0-to-1 products, new markets, or building new motions within an existing company
  • Ability to move between strategic planning and hands-on execution, comfortable with ambiguity and bias toward action
  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills; adept at influencing across Sales, Product, and Marketing
  • Deep experience with customer segmentation, positioning, pricing, and GTM planning
  • Experience in insurtech, SMB, fintech, HR/benefits/payroll tech, or a complex multi-audience business is a plus
  • AI fluent: has built AI workflows for research, content, or reporting and uses them to change how a team works

Compensation

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $153,000 - $187,000/yr in Denver and Atlanta, and $180,000 - $221,000/yr for San Francisco and New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.
